bearings.paper_claim: O(m log^(2/3) n) beats Dijkstra's O(m + n log n) only on sparse graphs, for single-source distances to ALL vertices on directed graphs with real non-negative weights, in the comparison-addition model. The analysis runs on a constant-degree transform with O(m) vertices and edges (m = O(n)). It returns distances without a full ordering; Dijkstra is optimal when the ordering is required (HHR+24). The constant C in Lemma 3.12 is not quantified and nothing is implemented.
bearings.paper_location: Abstract and Theorem 1.1, p. 1; Sec. 1, p. 1 (HHR+24); Sec. 2-3.1, pp. 3-4; Lemma 3.12, p. 14
bearings.system_side: The default office route is a point-to-sink search on an undirected hop graph: bidirectional Dijkstra with heuristic 0 that stops once the frontier lower bounds pass the best meeting (docstring :12-21; ALGORITHM :79). A second pass (_fewest_steps_exact, :436-480) solves the settled nodes in exact integers by scaling dyadic floats. Yen loopless alternatives need repeated searches. _search_reference (:266-298) is a one-way test oracle only. Not in the code: the 2026-10-02 latency lane (memory file, not code) found pair_cache grew the sidecar from 7.0 to 17.5 GB, i.e. memory, not heap cost; ALT landmarks deferred.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Carries over only if the system needs full single-source distance fields over the staffer graph (one origin to every office). The graph size is not established here: the ~4.66M figure traces to the co-tenure GUARANTEED pair count (4,660,388, staffer-sorting memory), which is an edge count, so the analyst's n ~ 10^6-10^7 is unsupported. The asymptotic ratio vs Dijkstra is about log^(1/3) n (roughly 2.5-3x for n in 10^6-10^7) before an unknown constant. Does not carry over to early-stopping point-to-sink, bidirectional, Yen or exact-tie passes, and does not touch the measured memory bottleneck. No recommendation to change the router.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper side confirmed (abstract; HHR+24 in Sec. 1; m = O(n) at start of Sec. 3.1; transform in Sec. 2). Code confirmed. Corrected: the staffer hop graph is undirected (docstring :3), the memory diagnosis comes from the latency-lane memory file not the code_ref, and the 4.66M / n ~ 10^6-10^7 size claim was not grounded as a vertex count.

bearings.paper_claim: Assumption 2.1 (all paths have distinct lengths) is made WLOG by ordering each path as the tuple <length l, vertex count alpha, vertices read from the end v_alpha..v_1> lexicographically, comparable in O(1) using Pred[] and alpha stored per bd[v]. The paper notes this is done like in many shortest-path papers.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 2, Total order of Paths, Assumption 2.1, p. 4
bearings.system_side: Staffer routes: costs within one part in 10^12 of the cheapest are ties; among them fewest steps wins, then least exact cost, then smallest node ids read from the sink end (D-082, Paul 2026-10-03).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Analogous, not identical: the paper compares exact length first and uses vertex count only on exact ties; the system lets a 1e-12 relative cost band count as a tie and then puts steps BEFORE exact cost. Both read the vertex sequence from the end. The paper's order is a presentation device for its own analysis and does not validate the system's tolerance band or step-first rule.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper text confirmed (Assumption 2.1 passage). Code docstring and D-082 (brain DECISIONS.md:692) confirmed. 'Matches' and 'supports, moderate' overstated: the orders differ in the tolerance band and in step-before-exact-cost; downgraded to context/weak. Lines 293-298 are the reference oracle, removed from code_ref.

bearings.paper_claim: The result is for real weights in the comparison-addition model. For integer weights in the word RAM model, the related-work line culminates in Thorup's O(m + n log log min{n, C}) for directed graphs [Tho04], where C is the maximum edge weight.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 1.2 Related Works, pp. 2-3 (Tho04; 'C is the maximum edge weight', highlighted by Paul, p. 3)
bearings.system_side: Overlap-route distances are integers: distance_units = max(1, ceil(1e6 x 128 / strength)) (:33-34), and the work_time variant max(1, ceil(1e6 / strength)) (:211). The search is bidirectional Dijkstra over heap keys (:140-165).
bearings.transfer_conditions: With integer weights the tighter asymptotic line is integer/word-RAM SSSP (Thorup), not this paper. Matters only if overlap-route latency becomes heap-bound, which has not been shown.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper Sec. 1.2 confirmed (word RAM, Tho04, C = max edge weight). Code confirmed; DISTANCE_SCALE = 1_000_000 at :27; work_time cost at :211 lacks the x128 factor (added to system_side).

bearings.paper_claim: Dijkstra's O(m + n log n) is beaten only asymptotically on sparse graphs, for a directed graph with non-negative weights; the paper assumes every vertex is reachable from s.
bearings.paper_location: Abstract and Theorem 1.1, p. 1; Sec. 2, pp. 3-4
bearings.system_side: distToTarget is a heap-free max-product Dijkstra scanning an array over N = 533 members, O(N^2); tracePath greedily follows PE[cur][v] x dT[v]. PE is directed: EMU[v] (receiver) enters PEBASE[u][v] (:586) and source_shock(u)/target_resistance(v) enter PE[u][v] (:595-597), so PE[u][v] != PE[v][u] in general.
bearings.transfer_conditions: At n = 533 the asymptotic gain is irrelevant. The paper adds nothing to reliability semantics (-log p) or the unestimated ASKM lift. Relevant only as a reminder that directed SSSP must relax edges in the query direction (see the distToTarget flag).
bearings.verifier_note: Code at :586, :591-597, :734-757 confirmed. Second reading of the analyst's flag: distToTarget seeds d[t]=1 and relaxes d[v]=d[u]*PE[u][v], i.e. best product over paths t->...->v, while tracePath scores PE[cur][v]*dT[v] as if dT were reliability v->...->t. With asymmetric PE this is the reversed direction; the PROVABLY-OPTIMAL comment (:735-737) holds only for symmetric PE. Reproduced by code reading only, not by a run.

related.why: The dashboard comment (make_dashboard_html_00.tpl:738) cites Chen, Shi, Zhang & Lam 2016 for most-reliable-path theory. Chen maximizes on-time arrival probability under a travel-time budget with stochastic link times (MRP-TS), not the dashboard's product of independent per-edge probabilities; Duan only bounds exact deterministic SSSP cost.
Empirically compares Dijkstra, A*, BFS and Greedy Best First on small 2D grids; covers the heuristic/goal-directed family that Duan's exact worst-case result does not.

Multi-Objective Path-Based D* Lite (incremental multi-objective replanning) covers dynamic and multi-objective cases that Duan's static single-objective SSSP does not. The analyst's claim that it is cited for a Pareto cosponsor route finder was not found in fec/surfaces.

Compares hop-count Dijkstra with an influence-based strongest path on directed weighted social ties, the modelling side Duan leaves out. Its tie strengths are heuristic model inputs, not access or introduction probabilities (D-025).

summary_issues: 'The one real link is Assumption 2.1 ... which matches the staffer router's (cost, steps) tie rule' overstates: the paper orders exact length, then vertex count, then reversed vertex sequence; the router (D-082) uses a 1e-12 relative tie band and puts fewest steps before least exact cost. Analogous, not matching.
The staffer hop graph is undirected (staffer_closeness_routes.py docstring); the paper's directed result covers it only as a special case.
The 'memory not heap' latency finding comes from the 2026-10-02 latency-lane memory file, not from the cited code lines.
Bearing transfer text gives a '~4.66M-pair staffer graph' and n ~ 10^6-10^7; 4,660,388 is the co-tenure GUARANTEED pair (edge) count, so the vertex scale is unsupported.
The distToTarget direction flag is reproduced by this verifier's code reading (second path, reading only); it remains unrun and is unrelated to the paper.

Chen 2016 related link: Chen solves on-time-arrival probability under a time budget, not the dashboard's max-product per-edge reliability, so 'supplies the semantics' is inaccurate. Ren 2022 link: the 'Pareto cosponsor route finder' citation was not found in fec/surfaces.
Paul's bib STOC 2025 (pp. 36-44, doi 10.1145/3717823.3718179) cannot be verified from the arXiv v2 text; cite arXiv:2504.17033v2.
